content.text:
Both the dashboard and the alert rule now exist in Kibana.

**Data view:** `Kibana Sample Data Logs` (`kibana_sample_data_logs`, time field `timestamp`). The fields that matter here are `response` (with a `response.keyword` subfield), `clientip`, `geo.dest`, `request`, `extension`, and `bytes`. I didn't get any actual values back from the data. The ES|QL and console proxy endpoints returned 404/400 in this environment, so I didn't check response-code distributions or the real time span of the data.

**Dashboard: `EFF-90bc2e92 Web logs overview`**
- Dashboard ID: `eff-90bc2e92-web-logs-overview-ba89291b0912`
- Five panels: total requests (count), unique client IPs, requests by response code, requests over time (date histogram), and top destination countries (`geo.dest`).
- Time range is the last 10 years, so the 2018-era sample data falls inside it. I chose this because I didn't confirm the data's actual dates. You may want to narrow it.

**Alert rule: `EFF-90bc2e92 5xx spike`**
- Rule ID: `403b564e-2d00-49be-95fd-3115b12b1e61`, type `.es-query`, consumer `stackAlerts`.
- Runs every 1m. Counts documents over the last 5 minutes where `response.keyword` matches `5??` (any three-character code starting with 5). Fires when the count is greater than 10.
- I created it enabled, since a rule that checks every minute should be running. Its status currently reads `ok`.
- The rule has no action connector, so it will record alerts but send no notifications.
